subject: Latency sprint triage & tokens/sec A/B test plan
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Riley Chan <riley.chan@vectorcloud.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency sprint triage & tokens/sec A/B test plan

Hi Riley — great to meet today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get the side-by-side ramped quickly.

Call recap (high level):
- VectorCloud goal: validate p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec for LLM-based summarization pipeline at 512 and 2048 prompt+context lengths.
- Hyperscaler baseline: you already ran quick tests with HypCloud v2 (no fine-tuning) and saw p95 ~ 220ms / p99 ~ 410ms at 512 tokens (no KV cache).
- Success criteria: p95 improvement >= 15% at 512; tokens/sec within 10% of baseline for 2048.

Proposed A/B probe (action items):
1) Scope: two workloads — Summarize (avg input 480 tokens) and Long Context (avg input 1,900 tokens).
2) Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU util, and steady-state variance over 30-minute runs.
3) Test matrix: Redwood tuned runtime (quantized variant) vs HypCloud v2; sequence lengths 512 and 2048; batch sizes 1, 4, 8.
4) Test harness: we will run our runner against your test account; you’ll provide a short sample corpus and an API key for HypCloud if you want them included in the same run.
5) Timeline: propose smoke runs this week (Wed/Thu PDT), full 30-minute sweeps Fri AM.

Attachments: redwood-hyperscaler-ab-probe-specs.pdf (test spec) and token-workload-profiles.csv (sample workload).

Ask: please confirm acceptance of the test matrix and share a preferred window for Wed/Thu. Also confirm whether we should include your internal HypCloud credentials in the same run or run independently and compare results.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0136

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Riley Chan <riley.chan@vectorcloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency sprint triage & tokens/sec A/B test plan

+1 on the matrix. A few technical notes from infra so expectations are aligned:
- For 2048 tokens we recommend enabling KV cache and using our quantized fp16-compatible runtime to keep memory in check. That will change the p95 behavior for long contexts (improvement is usually larger there).
- We’ll instrument the run with per-request timing and provide a CSV with token-level timing. Expect ~10–15% noise on short 5-minute runs; that’s why the 30-minute steady-state is important.
- Proposed runner: we’ll use the Redwood harness (attached spec). We need a dedicated test API key for VectorCloud (read-only) so we can trigger the HypCloud runs and collect metrics centrally. If you prefer to run HypCloud locally and share logs, we can ingest those as well.

Availability: We have a slot Wed 2026-05-20 09:00–11:00 PDT for smoke tests and Fri 2026-05-22 08:00–12:00 PDT for full sweeps.

I’ll prepare a simple script to push the workload and a short checklist (warmup, cache priming, steady-state start) so runs are comparable.

-- Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Riley Chan <riley.chan@vectorcloud.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency sprint triage & tokens/sec A/B test plan

Thanks — this looks good and matches what we discussed. Quick clarifications from our side:
- We can provide a read-only HypCloud test key for the runs; prefer you run both Redwood and HypCloud from your harness to reduce variability.
- On success criteria: can you confirm how you measure tokens/sec? Is it aggregated per-second across all workers or per-request tokens/sec? We want to ensure apples-to-apples.
- Cost: we’re sensitive to testing costs. If a full 30-minute sweep across matrix runs is expensive on our side, can Redwood run the HypCloud tests in our account and bill us for the consumed test minutes after the fact?

We can take the smoke slot Wed 20 May 09:00 PDT. I’ll upload the sample corpus to the Drive link and send the HypCloud key to priyom securely.

— Riley
Riley Chan
Lead ML Engineer, VectorCloud
riley.chan@vectorcloud.com

---

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Riley Chan <riley.chan@vectorcloud.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency sprint triage & tokens/sec A/B test plan

Perfect — thanks for confirming the slot. Quick answers inline:  
- tokens/sec measurement: we’ll report both per-request tokens/sec (request length / request latency) and cluster aggregate tokens/sec (total tokens processed / elapsed wall time). We’ll include both in the CSV so you can pick the comparator that maps to production.
- billing for runs: happy to run HypCloud tests in your account and provide an itemized usage report. We’ll estimate cost up-front based on run count; if you approve we’ll proceed and bill via the HubSpot deal.

Nexts:
- Riley: drop the HypCloud API key to priyom via the secure link you mentioned and upload corpus to the Drive folder.
- Priyom/Karthik: prep harness and smoke scripts for Wed 09:00 PDT. I’ll join to validate results and capture p95/p99.

See you Wed.

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
